reviews.title: Frustrating
reviews.text:
1) In the app store version, you must provide CC before even looking at the free trial.
2) after setting up the boat, home port, etc. I  tested the auto route feature for a  16 mile route I have taken many times. First attempt told me 19hrs. @ 30kts. Second attempt wanted me to pull my boat out of the canal designated as home port, trailer it 2 miles away to a canal it liked better and start from there, turning a 16 mile trip into 19.9 miles.
3)Weather information is not available for your area. Odd, as it's available in all my other apps... SW Florida is not a remote area with connectivity issues.

reviews.title: App is unstable and crashes repeatedly
reviews.text: The application crashes and reloads when doing simple tasks like zooming in on a chart or making a simple route.  Same results on PC and iPhone.   I do get a slow connection error (both on WiFi and 5G),  that I don’t get on any other apps.  I suspect Savvy Navvy is housed either on an underperforming server or in a remote location.  I’m currently in Florida, USA.   Novel concept for the app,  simpler than the big boys,  but unfortunately not ready for production.

reviews.title: Dodgy
reviews.text: 4 days trial pushed by RYA Day skipper online and then 99 quid charge. I should have cancelled it but feels expensive and scammy.

reviews.title: Crashed on a crossing.
reviews.text: Loved this app for a year. Then it crashed during a crossing from the gulf of Maine. Cannot log back in and customer support does not exist. It took them 3 days to get back and can’t fix the issue. I was using a new iPad Pro with the m5. Frustrating to spend so much money on an app that fails at the most needed time. Thankfully I downloaded Aquamaps as a back up and that’s worked flawlessly. Very frustrated.

reviews.title: Useless unless you pay
reviews.text: $123 a year is stupid. If you want to charge that much you need to get on salt strings level of detail and value.  Yes they have a free version but like the other reviews said the app is useless unless they have your card info. There are no contour lines at all for free and you can’t even get a satellite view for free might as well just use Google Maps. And there are no pricing details posted anywhere in the App Store so you don’t know what you are paying until you download and are forced to make a decision before even getting to look at what you are spending money on. Complete garbage

reviews.title: Premium not accessible
reviews.text: Purchased via iPhone. Worked. Spent over 5 hours attempting to add onto iPad mini (both ios 26.6.1). Seems to force UK version. Not an issue with linking to macbook air. Last contact with company "seems like a glitch". Perhaps they will get back to me& I will update. But paying $129 for one year & not being able to use these essential features on the device at the helm is a bit infuriating.

reviews.title: Hidden paid service
reviews.text: The app shows up first in search for 'free sea navigation app'. The app is in fact not free. False advertising, not even freemium.

reviews.title: Scammy phishy is a more fitting name
reviews.text: Signed up for the 3 day free trail. Only lets you create routes from your current location and never sends email or other confirmation of trial or when you cancel. Contacting their support is beyond sketchy as they ask for your email and other contact info to sell.

reviews.title: Don’t bother
reviews.text:
This is a big disappointment for me. I don’t know why they don’t tell you this before you download the app, but the app is worthless without giving your credit card first. To be able to use the app at all you have to give your credit card first and it gives you a three day free trial before it charges your credit card.  Deleted app immediately.  

App should be transparent, and I would tell people before they download the app exactly what to expect.  I would let you try it for a week at minimum so that if you download the app during the early work week, you can at least make it to the weekend to get out on the water at least and try this app out.

reviews.title: Not the Google Maps of Boating
reviews.text: The app lacks information, is not intuitive, and is overall lacking for a boating navigation tool. I subscribed to the premium subscription and regret paying for it. I have contacted support twice and they are not helpful. I recently asked about depth measurements for Moosehead Lake in Maine and was curtly informed they don’t have depth measurements for the lake. It’s the largest lake in the Northeast.

reviews.title: Location is not accurate
reviews.text: Current location is showing 200 meter which is showing I am on road while I am in the see

reviews.title: Numerous errors
reviews.text: We are new to boating world and really had high hopes for SV. The positives - very quick & easy to check wind, waves & tides. However, we are finding directions over land, ignoring recommended CTS, taking us through difficult waters that should be avoided, wrong side of cardinals & buoys & substantially incorrect distance and times. Other times it can show a perfect route, making the inconsistency more treacherous. We have fedback several times and been assured our issues are being addressed (“moved to latest algorithm”) but the issues keep coming. We expected this to be a modern replacement for old fashioned paper charts but we have to check everything with Chat GPT & Gemini first. It could be excellent, but it isn’t. Beware!

reviews.title: Data collection
reviews.text: This app tells you they are collecting any purchases you do on the device. All your searches & the data that goes with that. And there’s so much more. Why can’t we buy a service or device/app & it doesn’t take your location for another reason than to tell you where you are. I’m very disappointed that something as simple as a satnav would need to know what purchases I do on my phone. This is an overreach. And potentially something more than nefarious I personally feel.

reviews.title: Unstable on iPad
reviews.text: The title says it all. I create a route, select start and the App crashes, Up to that point it all looked very promising. I like the chart display.

reviews.title: AIS
reviews.text: Says it has ais but no targets show up. Atleast on the free version but I know for a fact vessels were within the two mile free version and nothing showed up. Even the vessel I’m on wouldn’t show up. Don’t advertise AIS if it don’t work.

reviews.title: Problems with offline map downloads
reviews.text:
The app is kinda cool - esp the passage planning. Obviously for on the water you need to download offline maps but for some reason they only down load 90% or so of the app. I’ve tried different wifis (at friends houses) and on mobile data but still can’t get 100%. 

I want to give the app 5* but it’s hard without the map data.  If the map is missing 5% of underwater hazards  and I hit one then…
